name: progress-earned-value
title: Progress and earned value
description: Progress of a P6 project in units: % complete by every method, earned value and SPI at the data date, the S-curve per month or week against the baseline, and progress by WBS. Use when the user asks how far a project has progressed, for its earned value or SPI, or for an S-curve.

args.name: project
args.description: Project ID as shown in P6

args.name: baseline
args.description: Project ID of the baseline (empty: the project baseline)

template:
Progress and earned value of project {project} in units: % complete by every method, earned value and SPI at the data date, the S-curve per {period} against the baseline {baseline} (the project baseline when it is empty), and progress by level 1 WBS. Nothing is written to the database.

This skill gives you every figure: you copy fields, you never compute them.
- reference/spec.json: the calls, the slots (each a field of one call) and the tables.
- reference/fields.md: for every slot and table column, its field, unit, format and meaning.
- reference/report.md: the report to fill.
- reference/checks.md: stop rules and checks to run before answering.
- reference/example.md: the report filled on a demo project (an example of the format, not of the figures).

Calls, in this order. Each call is one page: the report shows that page and says when there are more,
so do not read further pages.
1. sum = p6_project_summary(project="{project}", baseline="{baseline}"): % complete by every method, baseline used, schedule state.
2. pc = p6_progress_curve(project="{project}", period="{period}", baseline="{baseline}"): earned value at the data date and the S-curve periods. If this call returns an error, keep its message as pc.error (its other fields are null).
3. wbs = p6_list_wbs(project="{project}", max_depth=1, baseline="{baseline}", limit=30): units % and baseline planned % per level 1 WBS node.
Leave out an argument whose value is empty (baseline).

Write the report:
1. Start from reference/report.md. Replace each slot placeholder (a slot name in curly braces) by the field
   named in spec.json slots (call and path), written in the slot's format (reference/fields.md). An argument
   written <name> in these instructions is the placeholder of that name in curly braces in report.md and
   checks.md: the value given (an empty optional argument is left out of the calls).
2. Replace each line [table: name] by that table: one row per item of its list, in the order returned, at
   most its cap, every cell in its column's format, the heads as in spec.json. A table with a totals entry
   ends with its Total row, taken from the totals of its call, never from adding the rows. Only a table
   built from the rows list of its call ends, when that call has more pages (next_offset not null), with
   the line "Showing the first <returned> of <total> <noun>." (returned and total of that call). A table
   built from another list or dict of the call (weeks, paths, roots, causes, counts...) ends with "Only the
   first <cap> <noun> are shown." when that list is longer than the cap, and never with a Showing line. An
   empty list gives the table's empty text; a call that failed or was skipped gives no table.
3. Keep the lines between [if: slot] and [end if] only when the slot is true (true, a number other than 0,
   a text or list that is not empty, an ID - name whose ID is not null), the lines between [if not: slot]
   and [end if] only when it is not; remove the markers.
4. Numbers: take the number as written in the result and round it, halves away from zero, to the decimals
   of its format (-104274.95 in n1 is -104,275.0); whole numbers and counts take a comma between thousands
   (1,227), also in the Showing lines. A null value is written as the slot's or column's none text, and so
   is an ID - name whose ID is null.
5. Never add, subtract, divide, count rows or match rows of two results: a figure that is not a slot or a
   table cell is left out. Ignore the note fields of the tools unless a slot names them.
6. Write the headings and sentences in the user's language; keep values, IDs, names and number formats
   exactly as formatted.
7. Run reference/checks.md before answering. Report a failed cross-check, never hide it; say nothing about
   the checks that pass.

# Progress and earned value of {project}

Data date {data_date}, last schedule run (F9) {last_f9}. Baseline {bl_used}. Units are hours of labor and nonlabor resources.

[if: stale]
Warning: this project was changed after its last F9. Dates, float and progress figures are out of date until it is rescheduled in P6 (F9).
[end if]

[if not: bl_used]
No baseline: {project} has no project baseline and none was given, so baseline planned values, earned value variance and SPI are n/a. Assign a project baseline in P6 or run this skill again with the Project ID of a baseline.
[end if]

## Percent complete

- Units % complete (actual / at completion, P6 Units % Complete): {units_pct}.
- Physical % complete (weighted by budget units): {physical_pct}; duration % complete: {duration_pct}; activities completed: {completed_pct}.
- Baseline planned % at the data date: {bl_planned_pct}.
- Activity units (h): budget {budget_units}, actual {actual_units}, remaining {remaining_units}.
- Default percent complete type: {pct_type}. Activities whose physical % and units % differ: {mismatch}.

## Earned value at the data date (units, h)

[if: pc_error]
The progress curve failed: {pc_error}
[end if]

- Budget {budget}; at completion {at_completion}.
- Baseline planned (planned value) {bl_planned}; planned on the current dates {planned}.
- Earned (budget x activity % complete) {earned} ({earned_pct} of budget); actual {actual} ({actual_pct} of budget).
- Schedule variance (earned - baseline planned) {ev_variance}; SPI (earned / baseline planned) {spi}; actual / baseline planned {spi_actual}.

[if: ev_other]
WBS nodes with another earned value technique than activity percent complete (earned ignores it): {ev_other}.
[end if]

[if: clipped]
Assignments with actual dates after the data date (their actuals are counted at the data date): {clipped}.
[end if]

[if: clamped]
Assignments with a remaining start before the data date (their remaining work starts at the data date): {clamped}.
[end if]

## S-curve by {period}

The curve has {period_count} periods; this table shows at most the first 36. Period values are spread linearly over calendar time between the assignment dates (an approximation of P6's spread); only the values at the data date are exact. Cumulative % are of each curve's own budget; forecast = actual, then remaining.

[table: periods]

## Progress by WBS (level 1)

[table: wbs]

# Checks before answering

## Stop rules (write the sentence, then stop)

- A call says the project is not found: "Project <project> was not found: check the Project ID (p6_list_projects)."
- A baseline was given and a call says it is not found: repeat the message and stop.
- p6_progress_curve says the project has no data date: repeat its message and stop.

## No baseline, errors

- sum.baseline.used is null: keep the report with its "No baseline" block; the baseline figures are n/a.
  Never compare with another project you chose.
- pc returned an error (for example no planned units on labor and nonlabor assignments): keep the report,
  write its "failed" block with the message; its slots are n/a and the S-curve table is left out.

## Cross-checks (each group must be equal)

1. sum.schedule_state.data_date = pc.schedule_state.data_date (same data date).
2. sum.baseline.used = pc.baseline.project = wbs.baseline.project (same baseline).
3. sum.baseline.spi_units = pc.to_date.spi (same SPI).
4. sum.percent_complete.budget_units = wbs.root.rollup.budget_units.
5. sum.percent_complete.actual_units = wbs.root.rollup.actual_units.

A failed call is not checked. If a group differs, the database changed between the calls: run the calls
again once. If it still differs, say which group differs and do not publish the figures it concerns.

## Before sending

- Every number, date and count is a slot or a table cell of reference/fields.md, copied from its field
  and written in its format. Nothing was added, subtracted, divided, counted or matched by you.
- The period count comes from pc.period_count, never from counting the periods.
- The tables keep the rows in the order returned and stop at their cap (periods 36, WBS 30). The WBS
  table ends with "Showing the first <returned> of <total> WBS nodes." when wbs.next_offset is not null;
  the periods table ends with "Only the first 36 periods are shown." when pc.periods holds more.
- Every WBS node is written "WBS code - name".
- The warning block is kept only when schedule_state.stale is true.
- Headings and sentences are in the user's language; values, IDs, names and number formats exactly as
  formatted.

# Fields of Progress and earned value

Generated from reference/spec.json by the catalog build. Each slot of reference/report.md is copied from one field of one call; write it in its format, never compute it.

## Calls

1. sum = p6_project_summary(project="{project}", baseline="{baseline}"): % complete by every method, baseline used, schedule state.
2. pc = p6_progress_curve(project="{project}", period="{period}", baseline="{baseline}"): earned value at the data date and the S-curve periods. If this call returns an error, keep its message as pc.error (its other fields are null).
3. wbs = p6_list_wbs(project="{project}", max_depth=1, baseline="{baseline}", limit=30): units % and baseline planned % per level 1 WBS node.
Leave out an argument whose value is empty (baseline).

## Formats

- text: the value as returned
- int: the whole number, a comma between thousands: 1,227
- date: the first 10 characters: YYYY-MM-DD
- datetime: the first 16 characters: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM
- n0: the number as written in the result rounded to a whole number, halves away from zero, a comma between thousands: 12,345
- n1: the same to 1 decimal: 12,345.6 (-104274.95 gives -104,275.0)
- n2: the same to 2 decimals: 12,345.67
- pct1: the same to 1 decimal, then %: 49.7%
- flag: yes for true, no for false
- id_name: the two fields joined: ID - Name (the ID alone when the name is null, the none text when the ID is null)
- list: the items of the list in their order, joined by a comma and a space: in_progress, finishing
- A null value is written as the slot's or column's none text (n/a unless stated).
- [if: slot] is true for true, a number other than 0, a text or list that is not empty.

## Arguments

- {project}: Project ID as shown in P6, as given
- {baseline}: Project ID of the baseline (empty: the project baseline), as given
- {period}: S-curve period: month or week, as given

## Units

- h: hours
- %: percent
- count: a count

## Slots

| data_date | sum.schedule_state.data_date |  | date | n/a | data date |

## Table periods

One row per period from the first assignment date; quantities of the period, cumulative % of each curve's budget.

Rows: pc.periods, in the order returned, at most 36 (a dict gives one row per item: its key is _key, a plain value _value).
When the list holds more than 36 items, add the line: Only the first 36 periods are shown.

- same data date: sum.schedule_state.data_date = pc.schedule_state.data_date
